messages:
cs_zoe: FYI: Customer ACME ~prod reports persistent 503s hitting /v1/generate since ~03:20 UTC. They say some requests are charging twice in billing portal. Attaching sample req-id: req_0a1b2c3d. Error rate ~18% across 3 pods. Can oncall pick this up?

maya_oncall: on it. Can you paste a failing request id + any client logs? Do we have any recent deploys to hosted-runtime? @infra-bot any automatic rollouts? :eyes:

cs_zoe: client sent curl and response dump for req_0a1b2c3d (short):
```
POST /v1/generate
> 200ms -> 503 Service Unavailable
{"error":"upstream inference worker exited abruptly"}
```
They also included a stack-like snippet from our gateway: `upstream: stream closed (code=11)`, and a customer trace showing `context-length=40960`.

infra-bot: deploy: No customer-facing deploys in the last 4h. Autoscaler: scaled +1 pod at 02:55 UTC then stabilized. Node maintenance: none.

sam_runtime: grabbing logs from the affected pods now. Quick note: I see repeated `SIGSEGV` and `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` in runner logs for pod hosted-runner-42. Excerpt:
```
[2026-03-16T03:21:02Z] runner: Allocating KV cache 2.3GB
[2026-03-16T03:21:02Z] runner: cudaMalloc returned out of memory
[2026-03-16T03:21:02Z] runner: segfault (signal 11) at 0x000000
[2026-03-16T03:21:02Z] watchdog: container restarted
```
Also seeing `context_len=40960` and batchsize spikes to 16 in same window.

deepa_research: hmm, ACME uses long-context summarization (40k tokens). We rolled quantized-mmap patch yesterday which changed memory pressure slightly. Could be a regression where KV cache growth + quant memory mapping is not freeing fast enough.

maya_oncall: good catch. Sam, can you confirm whether OOM is GPU-only or we also saw host OOM/killed? Any coredump?

sam_runtime: host memory is fine. No OOM killer events. GPU driver log shows `GPU watchdog: process died` before container restart. I dumped /var/log/nvlib for that GPU: `GPU panic: page fault`. No user-space coredump present but container terminated cleanly by docker after signal 9.

deepa_research: that pattern matches a kernel-level GPU page fault triggered by illegal memory access — often seen when KV prefetch + attention kernel hit unexpected boundary. Could be input tensor shape causing out-of-bounds.

maya_oncall: mitigation plan (short): 1) divert traffic for ACME to fallback model variant (cpu/quantized-smaller) 2) temporarily set per-customer max_context=32k 3) scale runner pool + add redwood-fallback routing 4) patch to runtime to clamp KV prefetch size ASAP. Sam, can you enact 1 and 2?

sam_runtime: doing 1 and 2 now. Command: `redwood route update --customer acme --model rdx-small-fallback --max-context 32768`

sam_runtime: route update applied, started draining affected pods and routed new requests to fallback. Error rate dropped from 18% -> 2% within 90s. Rolling restarts of three hot pods in the group to collect logs for repro.

cs_zoe: relaying to ACME support: "We've routed your traffic to a fallback model variant to stabilize requests; we're investigating root cause for GPU worker restarts. No double billing should occur for retried requests but we're auditing billing events now."

billing_ops: looking at billing audit for req_0a1b2c3d window. We see two meter events for that request id: one with status=fail and one retried with status=success. By policy retries are not double-charged; we bill only successful token output. We'll follow up with the customer and waive any disputed charges if they still see billing anomalies.

deepa_research: repro hypothesis: large context (>36k) + batchsize >=12 + quant-mmap enabled -> sporadic KV page fault during prefetch. Repro steps to test in staging: 1) deploy quant-mmap build v0.17.2 to staging runners 2) synthetic load with context 40k and batchsize 16 across 4 concurrent streams 3) monitor /proc/driver/nvidia and runner logs for `page fault`

sam_runtime: creating repro job in staging now. Command I used: `k8s run --image redwood/runner:v0.17.2 --env CONTEXT=40960 --BATCH=16 --replicas=4 --test replayer`

maya_oncall: if repro succeeds, we should hotfix: revert quant-mmap or add bounds-checking in attention MM kernel. Deepa, can you prioritize kernel guard?

deepa_research: will spin up a quick patch to clamp prefetch size and add assert in dev branch. If repro is reliable, we'll push emergency revert. ETA 2-4h for patch + build.

sam_runtime: staging job running. Early signs: after ~200 iterations one runner in staging shows `GPU page fault` and container restart. Captured pstack and kernel trace.

sam_runtime: attaching short debug snippet captured from staging run:
```
runner: kv_prefetch(size=24000000) -> memcpy -> segfault
kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=1824
```
This matches production failure pattern.

maya_oncall: good repro. Next steps: 1) rollback quant-mmap to previous stable on hosted-prod (to prevent more customer impact) 2) schedule emergency release with deepa's bounds-check patch 3) communicate RCA and billing confirmation to ACME. I'll coordinate with release.

cs_zoe: I'll send customer update in 15m with current mitigations and note billing team is auditing.

billing_ops: confirmed: no automatic double-billing will be issued. If customer disputes we'll credit them.

infra-bot: rollback: release-2026-03-15-quant-mmap reverted from hosted-prod at 04:12 UTC by maya_oncall. Canary health: stable after routing to fallback and rerouting traffic.

maya_oncall: rolling status: prod error rate dropped to baseline ~0.5% after rollback + routing. We'll keep the fallback for ACME until the patch is validated.

deepa_research: opened GH issue #4672 with repro logs and staging traces. Working on kernel guard PR now.

cs_zoe: thx all. I'll update ACME and close customer ticket once we confirm final patch and billing note. :thumbsup:

sam_runtime: followup: saved runner core dumps & driver logs to s3://redwood-debug/acme-gpupanics/3955554321/ for postmortem.

maya_oncall: closing loop: keep this thread if anything spikes. Good catch team. :clap:
